claims.text: FeCoNiCrAl feedstock with a particle size of 15–45 μm was used in prior HVAF-M3 studies.
Standard HVAF-i7 processing of 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock produces acceptable coating quality but insufficient thickness.
An optimal spray distance of 300–350 mm was demonstrated for MCrAlY coatings sprayed with the HVAF-M3 system.
Setting the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate spray distance to 300–350 mm will increase FeCoNiCrAl particle velocity.
The proposed HVAF-i7 parameter adjustment will increase particle kinetic energy during flight.
Increased particle kinetic energy will improve particle flattening upon impact.
Increased particle kinetic energy will improve particle-to-substrate bonding upon impact.
Higher particle velocity will promote more complete substrate impingement and reduce particle rebound.
Higher particle velocity will improve inter-particle bonding.
Reduced rebound and improved bonding will increase deposition efficiency.
The intervention will produce a statistically significant increase in FeCoNiCrAl bond-coat thickness relative to standard HVAF-i7 processing of 15–45 μm feedstock.
The thicker coating will preserve coating adhesion and integrity.
The intervention will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation despite the increase in particle velocity.
The intervention will remain effective during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective for deposition inside internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Excessive in-flight oxidation or substrate damage would limit the intervention's effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The proposed 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance appears geometrically incompatible with deposition on the interior wall of a 120 mm internal diameter, which provides at most about 60 mm of radial clearance. No specialized torch orientation or geometry is specified to reconcile these requirements.
